articles.title: Cowboys release QB Joe Milton, keep Sam Howell to backup Dak Prescott this season
articles.summary: Joe Milton spent last season as a backup in Dallas, and appeared in four games.
articles.body:
The Cowboys released the backup quarterback on Monday, ending his short tenure with the franchise. In a corresponding move, running back Emari Demercado was claimed by the Cowboys off waivers from Kansas City.

The New England Patriots selected Milton in the sixth round of the 2024 NFL Draft out of Tennessee. He spent his rookie season there, but only appeared in one game, and then landed in Dallas the following offseason.

In his one year backing up Dak Prescott with the Cowboys, Milton appeared in four games. He threw for 183 yards and a touchdown, with two interceptions, while completing 15 of his 24 attempts.

The Cowboys kept Milton and Howell on their 53-man roster on Sunday, along with Prescott. With Milton now gone, Howell will presumably be the backup for the Cowboys to start the season. The former North Carolina quarterback spent last season with the Seattle Seahawks, but was most recently a starter during the 2023 campaign with the Washington Commanders.

Prescott threw for 4,552 yards with 30 touchdowns and 10 interceptions last season, his 10th with the Cowboys. They went 7-9-1 and missed the playoffs for a second straight campaign.

The Cowboys will open the season against the New York Giants on Sept. 13.

articles.title: "Do something with your life": Patrick and Brittany Mahomes faced intense social media scrutiny as several controversies surrounded their family
articles.summary: NFL News: The weeks after Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs won Super Bowl LVII were supposed to be all about celebration. Instead, his family found it.
articles.body: The weeks after Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs won Super Bowl LVII were supposed to be all about celebration. Instead, his family found itself at the centre of several online controversies. From criticism aimed at Jackson Mahomes to backlash over a luxury gift for Patrick and Brittany's daughter, the attention quickly moved beyond the football field. Looking back now, these were stories from March 2023, not recent developments.Patrick Mahomes family faced social media scrutinyMuch of the attention focused on Jackson Mahomes, Patrick's younger brother and a prominent social media personality. During the Chiefs' Super Bowl celebrations, Jackson appeared briefly behind Patrick during a post-game interview and was criticised online for dancing in the background. He later apologised and moved away from the camera.The criticism continued during Kansas City's victory parade on February 15, 2023. Jackson shared footage of himself on stage with Patrick, writing, "Patrick and I just vibing at the parade!"The response was mixed. Some social media users felt Jackson was taking too much attention during a celebration centred on the team. Others criticised him more broadly, including comments such as, "Bro thinks he's on the team."Jackson also faced criticism after posting a photograph with his mother. Some commenters told him to "Get a job", despite his established career as a social media influencer. Another person wrote: "Do something with your life."Another viral moment involved Patrick Mahomes and a replica Vince Lombardi Trophy. A video appeared to show the quarterback handing the trophy to fans during the parade. The clip sparked criticism until it became clear that the object was a detailed replica made by a Chiefs fan and had been given to Mahomes.Tom Brady defended the celebration, saying: "Looks like appropriate parade behavior to me @PatrickMahomes."Brittany Mahomes backlash added to family dramaBrittany Mahomes also became a target of online criticism during the same period. Her celebrations following Patrick's victories had already attracted attention, and podcast host Joe Rogan later made a controversial comment about how people might treat her if she and Patrick divorced.Brittany responded sharply, writing: "Something about grown men talking s*** about someone's wife is real weird..."She followed it with another post that read: "Actually grown ass men hating on women in general is pathetic," which many interpreted as a further response to the discussion.Patrick and Brittany also faced criticism after sharing their daughter Sterling Skye's second birthday celebrations. The couple reportedly gifted her a Chanel purse valued at around $4,800. Some social media users questioned the decision, arguing that a luxury handbag was unnecessary for a two-year-old.Even Patrick's fashion choices became part of the conversation. He unveiled an Adidas sneaker colourway called "Family Time" for Sterling's birthday, but the design received mixed reactions online.Meanwhile, photographs of Patrick and Brittany at an NBA game prompted another wave of speculation, with some viewers reading too much into Patrick's expression.The most serious development involved allegations against Jackson concerning an incident at a Kansas City-area restaurant. A restaurant owner accused him of forcibly kissing her, while his lawyer denied the allegations and argued that the interactions needed to be viewed in their "proper context."These controversies belong firmly to 2023, when the Mahomes family was facing intense attention following the Super Bowl. They should not be presented as current events. What the period showed, however, was how quickly a championship celebration could turn into a wider social media storm for one of the NFL's most visible families.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Travis Kelce warned to ‘be careful’ as his post-NFL Hollywood plans leave the internet deeply divided
articles.summary: NFL News: Travis Kelce had already started looking beyond the football field in 2024, as the Kansas City Chiefs star spoke openly about his desire to explore Ho.
articles.body: Travis Kelce had already started looking beyond the football field in 2024, as the Kansas City Chiefs star spoke openly about his desire to explore Hollywood once his NFL career eventually ends. In an interview that year, Kelce admitted he was testing the waters in entertainment while still treating football as his priority. His comments drew plenty of attention online, with fans split over whether the tight end could make a successful transition to show business.Travis Kelce reveals plans to explore entertainment after the NFLThe remarks came during a 2024 interview with The Hollywood Reporter, when Kelce was spending time in Los Angeles and getting more familiar with the entertainment industry. At the time, the NFL star was still firmly focused on football, but he was also making an effort to understand what life beyond the sport might look like."It still is, and I'm out here in LA trying to get more comfortable in the entertainment world before we start back up with this football thing, knowing that that's my main focus in my life, and it'll always be that until I'm done playing," Kelce revealed.Kelce also made it clear that he was not treating acting as a simple extension of his celebrity status. He acknowledged that scripted entertainment was a new space for him and said he wanted to develop his own creative instincts rather than rush into projects."But I'm definitely still dabbling in the scripted world, the entertainment world and we'll see where that road takes me. I'm extremely excited, but at the same time, I know I'm a bit of an amateur in that world, so I definitely got to get comfortable and, I don't know, put my own creativity on it."His comments suggested a gradual approach. Rather than announcing a specific acting career, Kelce appeared interested in learning how the industry worked and finding opportunities that suited his personality.Travis Kelce's Hollywood ambitions spark mixed reactionsKelce was not exactly a stranger to entertainment by 2024. His 2023 appearance on Saturday Night Live gave viewers a chance to see his comedic side, while television commercials had already made him a familiar face outside the NFL.He had also expanded his profile through New Heights, the podcast he co-hosts with his brother Jason Kelce. The show had become an important part of his growing media presence and showed that his appeal could extend beyond game-day performances.Still, his Hollywood plans divided internet users. Some welcomed the possibility of seeing Kelce take on more entertainment projects, while others questioned whether success on a football field and popularity on television would translate into scripted acting.Social media reactions ranged from enthusiastic support to blunt skepticism. One Facebook user wrote, "Love him," while another offered a warning: "Oh boy Travis. Be careful."The debate was understandable. Kelce had already built a major public profile, but acting would require a different set of skills. His willingness to describe himself as an amateur also showed that he understood the difference.Since the original story was published in April 2024, Kelce's comments should be viewed as an account of his ambitions at that time, rather than a new 2026 announcement. What made the story notable was his early interest in building an entertainment career before eventually stepping away from professional football.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders welcome Savanna Dastrup after heartbreaking rejection nearly ended her dream
articles.summary: NFL News: For Savanna Dastrup, becoming a Dallas Cowboys cheerleader was never a passing childhood wish. She first fell in love with the team at 14 after watchi.
articles.body: For Savanna Dastrup, becoming a Dallas Cowboys cheerleader was never a passing childhood wish. She first fell in love with the team at 14 after watching Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders: Making the Team with her mother. One failed audition could have ended that dream, but the Orem High School graduate returned stronger, earned her place and is now preparing to step onto the field in Dallas.Savanna Dastrup turns Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders rejection into motivationDastrup knows better than most that making the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders requires more than talent. It demands discipline, resilience and the willingness to keep showing up when the outcome does not go your way.She auditioned for the team in 2025 and made it through training camp. Then came the setback she had feared. She was cut just one week before the final team was announced.The experience hurt, but it also gave her a reason to push harder.“I actually auditioned last year, made it through training camp and got cut, like, the week before the team was made,” Dastrup said. “It was super hard, super devastating. But it really motivated me to come back and work harder. And it meant that much more.”Instead of treating the rejection as the end of her journey, Dastrup decided to use it as fuel.“I wasn’t going to stop either,” Dastrup said. “If it wasn’t this year, I was going to audition again.”That determination eventually paid off. She made the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders this year and is now preparing for her first appearance in front of Cowboys fans.The achievement still feels surreal to her.“I can’t even believe it still,” Dastrup said. “I’m so used to coming and being like, ‘Am I going to get cut tonight?’ I think I still am trying to get out of that mindset. Like, Savanna, you made it.”Her journey began years earlier, when her mother introduced her to the popular reality series following the cheerleaders' auditions and training.“My mom was like, ‘You should watch Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders: Making the Team with me,’” Dastrup said. “So I watched it and I was like, ‘That’s what I want to do.’ From there, I was like, ‘Please, we have to go to a Cowboys game.’”That early fascination eventually became a serious goal.Dallas Cowboys cheerleader Savanna Dastrup credits family for her successWhile determination brought Dastrup back after rejection, she says her family gave her the foundation to keep pursuing the dream.Her father taught her the value of putting in extra work, a lesson that became especially important after her first audition ended in disappointment.“You fight and earn for your spot every single day,” she said. “My dad always told me to be the first at the studio, the last to leave - put in the extra work - and what’s meant to be will be.”Her Utah roots have also remained an important part of her journey.“Utah is definitely my rock,” she said. “I have the best supportive family, and I couldn’t be more grateful. And I think support was the biggest thing.”Now, that support system is preparing to make the trip to Texas to see Dastrup live out the dream she has carried since she was a teenager.“I don’t think my parents will miss a game,” Dastrup said. “Family, friends, everyoneI’m like, ‘Come on, everybody come to Texas.’”Even before her official debut, she can already feel the excitement building. Hearing “Thunderstruck” during practice gives her butterflies, and she expects the emotion to be even stronger when the music plays inside the stadium.“I would not be surprised if I had tears running down my face of happiness and joy the first time I do it,” she said.But perhaps the most meaningful part of Dastrup's story is what she hopes other young women take from it.“I hope that girls that get rejected or don’t make the team they want realize there is a bigger picture,” she said. “And just, yeah, don’t give up.”For Dastrup, those words are not simply advice. She has lived them. Her first rejection did not erase the dream. It made the moment she finally earned her Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders spot even more meaningful.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Patrick Mahomes sends heartwarming message to Brittany Mahomes on her special day as Chiefs star shares intimate family moments
articles.summary: NFL News: Patrick Mahomes had a simple way of making Brittany Mahomes’ 31st birthday feel special. The Kansas City Chiefs quarterback turned to Instagram with a.
articles.body: Patrick Mahomes had a simple way of making Brittany Mahomes’ 31st birthday feel special. The Kansas City Chiefs quarterback turned to Instagram with a collection of personal family moments, offering fans a glimpse into the bond they have built away from football. From memories at home to time with their three children, the birthday tribute focused on the relationship that has grown alongside Mahomes’ remarkable NFL career.Patrick Mahomes shares heartfelt birthday message for Brittany MahomesMahomes marked his wife’s birthday by sharing several snapshots from their life together. The photos included a sweet picture of the couple outside their home and a family moment featuring their children, Sterling, Bronze and Golden.Rather than writing a long birthday post, the Chiefs star kept his message short and deeply personal."Happy Birthday! ❤️ Love you Forever ❤️,"The message quickly drew a loving response from Brittany, who shared the same sentiment in the comments."I love you forever 🥹🤍,"The exchange offered a softer look at the couple, whose relationship has remained a familiar part of Mahomes’ public life. Their story began long before his NFL stardom. The two met while attending high school in Texas and started dating during their teenage years.They eventually took the next major step in their relationship, getting married in Hawaii in March 2022. Since then, their family has continued to grow, with Sterling, Bronze and Golden becoming an important part of their shared life.Brittany Mahomes celebrates 31st birthday in styleWhile Patrick Mahomes chose to celebrate his wife through a family-focused tribute, Brittany gave followers a closer look at her birthday festivities.The 31-year-old shared photos from her celebration, including a striking outfit that brought a polished touch to the evening. She wore a white long-sleeved jacket with a matching mini skirt, paired with knee-high denim-blue boots. Patrick also joined the celebration in a coordinated khaki outfit with a white T-shirt.Brittany kept her caption brief, letting the pictures do most of the talking."3️⃣1️⃣🫶🏼,"One of the standout moments showed her posing against a gold backdrop decorated with a balloon arch and large balloons marking the number 31.The birthday weekend also gave the couple an opportunity to step away from their busy routine. Patrick and Brittany travelled to Las Vegas to watch the Backstreet Boys perform at The Sphere, adding a memorable night out to the celebrations.For the Mahomes family, the weekend was less about grand gestures and more about spending time together. Patrick’s Instagram tribute and Brittany’s birthday snapshots offered fans a glimpse of that balance, with family, romance and celebration taking centre stage.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: First-time voters can apply to be on SIR list by September 30 in Maharashtra
articles.summary: MUMBAI: The draft voter li­st of Maharashtra’s special int­e­nsive revision, pu­b­lished on Monday, has 2 cr­o­re fewer voters than the previous elect.
articles.body: MUMBAI: The draft voter li­st of Maharashtra’s special int­e­nsive revision, pu­b­lished on Monday, has 2 cr­o­re fewer voters than the previous electoral roll. Mumbai is down by 36 lakh voters — a 35% fall.The electoral roll used ti­ll June had 9.8 crore voters, while the draft SIR roll has 7.7 crore voters, which is 21.1% lower. However, in real terms there are 1.9 crore fewer voters in the state on the draft list since 17 lakh voters were removed from one constituency owing to duplicati­on, but ha­ve been retained in the other. “The 17 lakh duplicate voters cannot be considered as excluded,” state chi­ef electoral officer S Chockalingam said.The reduction in voters is because their enumerati­on forms were not collected owing to them being reported as absent, shifted their residen­ce, dead or duplicate.Around 1.5cr of the 2cr vo­ters whose names have be­en excluded will have the opportunity to apply to be on the SIR list until Sept 30.This is the phase of filing claims and objections to the draft roll. First-time voters who turned 18 before Oct 1 can also apply to be on the SIR voter list during this one-month period till Sept.“Around 34 lakh voters were reported dead, while 17 lakh were related to duplicate registrations. Hence, around 1.5 crore of the 2 crore voters whose names have been excluded because they were absent or had shifted residence have the opportunity to apply to be on the electoral roll,” said Chockalingam.Citizens can check their names on the draft roll on the ECI portal and website of the state’s chief electoral officer as well as the website of the district election officers. The draft rolls are also available with recognised political parties at the district level.If citizens have been excluded from the list after they filled out the enumeration form and even if they have missed filling the enumeration form, they can fill out Form 6 to be included on the SIR voter list. They can also fill out Form 7 for deletion from the list and Form 8 for corrections in name, address, gender and so on.These forms can be filled out online on the above sites. Also, citizens can approach electoral registration officers in their assembly constituency — their addresses are on the website of the state’s chief electoral officer. Citizens can also approach booth level officers or block level agents appointed by political parties.Of the total 7.7 crore voters in the SIR draft list in the state, 3.9 crore are male and 3.7 crore female. Of the 2 crore voters who have not been included in the draft roll owing to uncollected forms, the highest numbers are from urban areas as a result of internal shifting and migration. While Mumbai had the highest number, the other key cities with exclusions were Pune (28.6 lakh), Thane (28.5 lakh) and Nagpur (14.4 lakh).You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Mumbai | Silver Rate in Mumbai | Bank Holidays in Mumbai | Public Holidays in Mumbai | Mumbai AQI | Weather in Mumbai | Petrol Price in Mumbai | Diesel Price in Mumbai | CNG Price in Mumbai | LPG Price in MumbaiStay updated with the latest Mumbai news. articles.title: B/R 99: Ranking the 99 Best Fantasy Football Seasons of All Time
articles.summary: When a fantasy manager lands a league-winning player, it's an event. A full season's worth of pure football joy and something to hold over leaguemates for years on end.
articles.body:
When a fantasy manager lands a league-winning player, it's an event . A full season's worth of pure football joy and something to hold over leaguemates for years on end.

It's one of the purest reasons to play this game we all love, allowing us to say, even if for just a short period: I made the better call.

Fantasy football is littered with these seasons in the decades since it became popular. To sort them all out, two-time Fantasy Sports Writers Association Football Writer of the Year Gary Davenport considered several factors, including total scoring in full-point-per-reception formats, average draft position, performance relative to positional peers and some good old-fashioned subjectivity from years in the fantasy game.

Since 1980, no one's done it better than this bunch.

Try the B/R Fantasy Picker and build your own all-time squad on a $15 budget.

The list kicks off with a grouping that features two of the lowest draft positions in our ranking. Baker Mayfield went 158th in 2024, and Cam Newton went 152nd in 2011. Each finished as QB3, which is roughly the bar for entry here.

Keep scrolling to explore the next tier.

Nine of the 10 players in this group had already finished among the top 12 at their positions the previous season. Most, however, were not the only players at their respective positions to post career years.

Still, this group is one of the clearest indicators that a player didn't have to win his position in a given year to make the list. Only four of these 10 did so, the fewest of any group from here on out.

The 1990s are well represented here: four of the 13 seasons from the magazine era (1987-98) land in this tier—Steve Young, Jerry Rice, Emmitt Smith and Barry Sanders.

It's also the tier with the most surprises, as Jimmy Graham, Steve Smith Sr. and rookie Edgerrin James were all off the fantasy radar the year prior.

There was lots of value to be had in this group. Seven of the 10 went off draft boards at pick 18 or later the year before, including 1999 Marvin Harrison after a WR32 season, 2017 Todd Gurley after finishing RB20 and 2021 Tom Brady following a QB8 finish.

There were exceptions, though, with 2021 Josh Allen, 2020 Travis Kelce and 2004 Tony Gonzalez all repeating as the top player at their respective positions.

Expectations were high in this group, and it turns out that drafters got it right. Six of the 10 went in the first 10 picks, and nearly all of them were top-12 at their position the year before.

This is also the most modern stretch in the rankings, as 2003 is as far back as this group goes.

No other tier covers more ground. It's the only one that touches all four eras of fantasy data, spanning from 1983 to 2025. The logic of the rankings shows in the spread, as 2022 Mahomes has the ninth-highest raw point total on the list, while the two tight ends sit in the 90s.

Position scarcity and era context carry as much weight here as anywhere on the board.

All 10 seasons in this group finished No. 1 at their respective positions, making it the first tier to feature a clean sweep—though not the last. In 1980, Kellen Winslow outscored the next-best player at his position by a larger margin than any other player on the list.

Speaking of that era, nearly half the list's pre-1987 entrants are packed into this group. Winslow, 1983 Eric Dickerson and 1985 Roger Craig make three of the seven representing fantasy's early days.

We arrive at the second consecutive group in which every player finished No. 1 at his position.

This time, the cost of admission varied wildly.

2015 Antonio Brown went third overall on average and 2001 Marshall Faulk went first, while 2011 Gronkowski (119) and 2015 Cam Newton (84) came off the board much later.

This tier illustrates the value that elite tight end and quarterback seasons can provide when managers identify breakout candidates at a discount.

This group features dominant seasons from a young Arian Foster in 2010 and a veteran Randy Moss in need of a change of scenery before his reemergence in 2007, both of whom were completely off the fantasy radar the previous year.

Elsewhere, both 2006 Steven Jackson and 2003 LaDainian Tomlinson were RB2 in those years, each finishing behind a player who had a top-10 season on our list.

Also of note, Dan Marino's 1984 is the earliest season in the top 20 and the highest ranked entry from before 1987.

The top 10 is exceptionally strong, and any one of these seasons could have delivered a fantasy league title. The five running backs in this tier were all top-five picks, underscoring the position's value. Even with that lofty draft status, they still exceeded expectations.

The other positions paint a different picture. The two quarterbacks in this tier—2018 Patrick Mahomes and 2019 Lamar Jackson—had ADPs near 100 and were afterthoughts the previous season. Cooper Kupp, the highest-ranked wide receiver, finished as WR34 in 2020 before his historic 2021 campaign.

2022 Kelce, the lone tight end in this group, ranked No. 87 in raw points among the 99 seasons. That was the largest disparity between a season's overall ranking and its raw-points ranking, illustrating the value of outperforming positional peers.

articles.title: Updated BR NFL1000 Team Rankings After 2026 Roster Cuts
articles.summary: The NFL's annual cutdown day is always difficult for everyone involved. Ultimately, the league's 53-man roster mandate is supposed to serve as a way to level the playing field, but not all active rosters are built the same.
articles.body:
The NFL's annual cutdown day is always difficult for everyone involved. Ultimately, the league's 53-man roster mandate is supposed to serve as a way to level the playing field, but not all active rosters are built the same.

Prior to the start of the preseason, Bleacher Report identified the league's most stacked rosters . A revisit was necessary after moves were made at this year's initial roster deadline.

Interestingly, the same 10 teams remain at the top. However, some of the positions shifted, with a noticeable trend in favor of those squads cutting graded players. Conversely, organizations that can move on from graded players demonstrate just how deep their rosters are.

The B/R NFL 1000 continues to serve as a barometer to determine which squads are the most talented based on how they're currently built. The following 10 teams have the highest concentration of top talent based on their average overall grade among those appearing on the list and how many of those individuals cracked B/R's Top 100.

Click here for a rundown of the full NFL 1000 series slate.

Average Grade : 71.8 Top 100 Players : 4 Highest-Rated : Josh Allen

Offensively, the Buffalo Bills know what they have. Quarterback Josh Allen is an annual MVP candidate. Running back James Cook Jr. returns as the league's leading rusher. DJ Moore was added to the mix this offseason, which increased the talent and depth at wide receiver. Buffalo's offensive line is experienced. The defense is primarily where question marks still exist. A lack of cornerback depth is concerning. Granted, CJ Gardner-Johnson and Jalon Kilgore present flexibility as safeties with plenty of experience covering the slot. Still, the team's pure cornerback options are thin at best. Furthermore, the transition to Jim Leonard's new scheme remains a work-in-progress. The Bills should be more aggressive overall. It's still not known whether all the right pieces are in place for this group to legitimately play strong complementary football.

Average Grade : 72 Top 100 Players : 4 Highest-Rated : Zach Frazier

The Pittsburgh Steelers will again hang their hat on a veteran-laden defense, with Cameron Heyward, T.J. Watt and Jalen Ramsey leading the way. The unit will also benefit from the investments made in Keeanu Benton, Nick Herbig, Jamel Dean and Jaquan Brisker.

The biggest changes to the roster from the start of training camp to the end of preseason came along the offensive line, where center Zach Frazier serves as the anchor.

Pittsburgh traded 2023 first-round pick Broderick Jones to the Dallas Cowboys after injuries clouded his future and the Steelers have a viable replacement in Troy Fautanu, who shifted from right to left tackle. The entire right side of the line will look different this fall.

Dylan Cook is expected to open the season at right tackle and hold down that spot until first-round rookie Max Iheanachor is ready. Spencer Anderson should be the new starting right guard as well. Even if some of the names are the same, three-fifths of the Steelers offensive line will be new this season.

Obviously, Pittsburgh has plenty of talent at multiple positions, but the Steelers could be held back by an aging quarterback playing behind a reworked front five.

Average Grade : 72 Top 100 Players : 5 Highest-Rated : Patrick Surtain II

The depth of a roster can often be ascertained by its rookie class. First-year players, particularly Day 3 draft picks, have a much harder time cracking a quality lineup.

Case in point, the Denver Broncos drafted seven players this past April. Three of them have already been cut. In fact, all but one of the team's draftees in the fifth round or later failed to make the roster.

The vast majority of Denver's roster returns from last season. The Broncos were one game away from making the Super Bowl. Significant changes weren't necessary. If anything, a young core of talent can continue to grow together.

Quarterback Bo Nix, running back RJ Harvey, wide receiver Troy Franklin, pass-rusher Nik Bonitto, safety Talanoa Hufanga and cornerbacks Patrick Surtain II, Riley Moss and Ja'Quan McMillian are all 26 or younger.

As that group develops, the Broncos expect bigger and better returns each season.

Average Grade : 72.2 Top 100 Players : 4 Highest-Rated : Jaxon Smith-Njigba

A pair of significant injuries could mar the early portion of the Seattle Seahawks' 2026 campaign. The organization already planned for one, but it doesn't necessarily have a fallback plan for the other.

Expectedly, Zach Charbonnet will open the season on the physically unable to perform list after suffering a torn ACL during the team's Super Bowl run. First-round rookie Jadarian Price will function as the Seahawks' lead back to open the campaign.

"He's done a great job. He really has—all three downs," head coach Mike Macdonald said, per ESPN's Brady Henderson . "He's a rookie in terms of, there's going to be things that we're going to attack in his game that will show itself in games. We haven't been afforded the luxury of having the bodies right now at running back to give him the reps in a [preseason] game that we would normally give to a rookie runner."

Conversely, last year's superstar rookie, Nick Emmanwori, may not be ready for Week 1 after requiring offseason ankle surgery. He is a legitimate difference-maker and valuable defensive piece thanks to his versatility. He can't be immediately replaced.

Otherwise, Sam Darnold moves into his second year as Seattle's starting quarterback. The squad's top wide receivers and starting offensive line remain intact. Maybe most importantly, the Seahawks' veteran defensive front still has Leonard Williams, Byron Murphy II and DeMarcus Lawrence to help dictate contests.

Four significant additions could change the face of this Baltimore Ravens squad (beyond the hire of head coach Jesse Minter).

Offensively, a pair of rookies should help to address significant need areas. The first-round selection of Olaivavega Ioane can provide a physical tone-setter along the offensive interior. With the loss of three-time Pro Bowl center Tyler Linderbaum in free agency, Ioane can now be the tip of the spear for Baltimore's front five.

Third-round wide receiver Ja'Kobi Lane was the most pleasant surprise from the Ravens' training camp. He is a big-bodied target to provide a different dynamic in the team's passing attack.

On the other side of the ball, Nnamdi Madubuike's expected return from a serious neck injury could provide a significant lift since he's one of the game's best interior pass-rushers.

Madubuike played in only two games last season before being sidelined. He's starting the 2026 campaign on Baltimore's active roster.

Finally, Trey Hendrickson's signing gives the squad the caliber of pass-rusher it's lacked for a long time.

Those four coupled with quarterback Lamar Jackson, running back Derrick Henry, tight end Mark Andrews, wide receiver Zay Flowers, linebacker Roquan Smith and safety Kyle Hamilton make the Ravens an AFC favorite if the group stays healthy.

Average Grade : 72.4 Top 100 Players : 6 Highest-Rated : Lane Johnson

Talent has never been in question with the Philadelphia Eagles. General manager Howie Roseman understands how to draft and stack a roster. This year's squad is all about whether the team actually jells. It didn't happen last season despite an 11-6 record and postseason berth. It's clear the Eagles have the capabilities of competing at a high level. High-end performers can be found throughout the lineup. Obviously, the AJ Brown trade changes the Eagles' aerial attack. However, the signing of Dontayvion Wicks and first-round selection of Makai Lemon give Philadelphia two more options beyond DeVonta Smith. Beyond signing Riq Woolen to upgrade the outside corner spot opposite Quinyon Mitchell, the Eagles have everything in place to succeed and possibly compete for another Super Bowl appearance. Even so, the team keeping four quarterbacks became the most interesting aspect coming out of training camp and the preseason. Jalen Hurts' erratic play proved to be rather limiting in 2025. The team now has veteran Andy Dalton and Tanner McKee backing up the incumbent. Plus Cole Payton is a developmental option. The Eagles are too talented overall to have their quarterback hold them back.

Average Grade : 72.4 Top 100 Players : 7 Highest-Rated : Jahmyr Gibbs

Even though the Detroit Lions now find themselves among the league's top four squads, the team did take a significant hit during training camp when center Cade Mays suffered a fractured wrist.

Mays is expected back this season after being placed on injured reserve with a designation to return. Still, his absence will be felt. Detroit features significant offensive talent, specifically quarterback Jared Goff, running back Jahmyr Gibbs and wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown. But the offense is built on a strong offensive line.

Now, the O-line is questionable. Penei Sewell is making the switch from right to left tackle. Rookie Blake Miller takes over at right tackle. The coaching staff was experimenting with options to take over at center leading into the regular season. Detroit did acquire Juice Scruggs, as part of the David Montgomery trade, to help offset the injury loss.

Beyond that specific concern, the Lions lineup is far better than last season's 9-8 record indicates. This group may not be 15-2 good, but it's likely closer to what it was two seasons ago than last year, mainly due to the hire of Drew Petzing as offensive coordinator and Kelvin Sheppard being more experienced as the defensive play-caller.

Average Grade : 72.8 Top 100 Players : 5 Highest-Rated : Myles Garrett

The Los Angeles Rams are a legitimate wild card in these rankings. They're ranked third without a designation for Aaron Donald, who just came out of retirement and re-signed with the team.

For transparency's sake, Donald wouldn't have received a grade from the B/R Scouting Department, because he hasn't played since the 2023 campaign. No one knows exactly the caliber of performer returning to the Rams. Though most expect him to be a quality performer once again, even if the 35-year-old is no longer competing to win a fourth NFL Defensive Player of the Year award.

There's a world where Donald is still an excellent player even if he takes a couple of steps back. If so, the Rams could realistically be the No. 1 team among these rankings. Even without him, the roster is loaded.

Myles Garrett is the No. 1 overall player on the B/R NFL 1000. Matthew Stafford is the league's reigning MVP. An argument can be made in favor of Puka Nacua as the game's top wide receiver. The defensive front also features Byron Young, Kobie Turner and Braden Fiske. Plus, general manager Les Snead upgraded the secondary this offseason with the acquisitions of Trent McDuffie and Jaylen Watson.

As a result, the Rams continue to receive significant Super Bowl hype and deservedly so.

Average Grade : 73 Top 100 Players : 6 Highest-Rated : Fred Warner

The San Francisco 49ers' regular-season roster benefited the most from new rankings. They moved from ninth to second after making cuts and nearly caught the No. 1 team. This movement shows how strong San Francisco's talent core really is.

The last point should come as no surprise. San Francisco has regularly featured some of the league's best rosters since John Lynch became general manager and Kyle Shanahan took over as head coach.

Injuries have been the franchise's bugaboo, and the 49ers defense will rely heavily on Nick Bosa, Mykel Williams and Fred Warner this year. All three are coming off of significant season-ending injuries. Conversely, the squad shouldn't count on Christian McCaffrey as much as last season. He's now 30 coming off a 400-plus-touch campaign.

The talent is readily available and obvious, with Brock Purdy, Trent Williams and George Kittle to go along with those already mentioned.

To the organization's credit, it still signed Mike Evans, re-signed Deebo Samuel and drafted De'Zhaun Stribling to rework the wide receiver room. Fourth-round rookie Carver Willis could be a first-year starter at left guard. Dre Greenlaw is back as well.

At the same time, a delicate balancing act (and a little luck) is necessary for the Niners to fully capitalize during this window.

Average Grade : 73.1 Top 100 Players : 6 Highest-Rated : Derek Stingley Jr.

The Houston Texans remain in the top spot after reducing their roster to the 53-man limit. But the organization wasn't content with what it already had on the roster. Instead, general manager Nick Caserio swung a pair of low-level but possibly significant trades at the deadline.

Obviously, the Texans will be built around their defense. Will Anderson Jr., Danielle Hunter, Derek Stingley Jr., Jalen Pitre and Calen Bullock are all standouts. No opponent wants to face this group. However, the Texans can't be considered legitimate contenders until their offense proves itself, starting with C.J. Stroud.

In order for the quarterback to thrive, the Texans did what they could to solidify their offensive line and improve his surrounding cast. This offseason, Houston brought in running back David Montgomery, as well as offensive linemen Wyatt Teller, Braden Smith and first-round rookie Keylan Rutledge. The team didn't stop there.

Caserio traded for wide receiver Kayshon Boutte and offensive tackle Nate Thomas this week. Boutte finished second on the New England Patriots last season with six touchdown receptions. He also averaged 16.7 yards per catch—which topped everyone on the Texans. Meanwhile, Thomas made four starts at left tackle for the Dallas Cowboys, giving Houston more experienced depth.

The Texans may be talented, but they haven't achieved anything of note. These types of fortifications are exactly what can keep a squad afloat and performing at a high level when its depth is challenged throughout a campaign.

articles.title: Texas State football: 5 things to know about Texas Longhorns in Week 1 matchup
articles.summary: Texas State football's 2026-27 season kicks off Saturday against the Texas Longhorns, perhaps its toughest matchup of the season.
articles.body:
Texas State football's 2026-27 season kicks off Saturday against the Texas Longhorns, perhaps its toughest matchup of the season. Texas coach Steve Sarkisian spoke to the media Monday, sharing his thoughts on his program's preparedness and Texas State's rising status through the college ranks.

"A ton of respect for GJ Kinne and the job he's done at Texas State," Sarkisian said. "They're elevated as a program. They're now in the Pac-12, and he's got a really good football team."

Here's what to know about the Longhorns before Saturday's game.

Four Longhorns might be selected in the first round of the 2027 NFL Draft.

That list starts with quarterback Arch Manning, the nephew of former NFL quarterbacks Eli and Peyton Manning . He struggled as a starter last year before finding his groove in the back half of the season, throwing for 3,163 yards, 26 touchdowns and seven interceptions while completing 61.4% of his passes. The Athletic's Nick Baumgardner has him going No. 1 overall in his preseason 2027 NFL mock draft.

Left tackle Trevor Goosby, edge rusher Colin Simmons and wide receiver Cam Coleman also are projected to go within the top 10 picks of the mock draft.

Texas fired defensive coordinator Pete Kwiatkoski after last season, hiring former South Carolina and Florida head coach (and also former UT defensive coordinator) Will Muschamp as his replacement.

The Longhorns speak highly of Muschamp, who demands physicality and accountability in his practices. Sarkisian has praised the coach's defensive mind and brought him in to field a "more aggressive defense." This entails fewer schemes designed to limit big plays and more press coverage designed to stop easy, short completions.

Sarkisian said that aggressiveness does not entail recklessness. Even so, he's not naive to the idea that the adjustment to the scheme might take some time.

"There'll be some growing pains, but that's OK, too. That's part of this process," Sarkisian said.

Texas took a step back in 2025, missing the College Football Playoff after two consecutive berths in 2023 and 2024. Sarkisian said Monday the previous year's roster was "probably a little too young around Arch." Texas responded by piecing together the No. 2-ranked transfer portal class, according to 247Sports' composite ratings.

Coleman highlights the group as a 6-foot-3, 201-pound wideout who can be Manning's true No. 1 target. The Longhorns also added two of the best running backs on the market - Hollywood Smothers and Raleek Brown - to bolster the rushing attack.

Linebackers Rasheem Biles and Justin Cryer were other huge wins after linebacker Anthony Hill Jr. left for the NFL.

Texas LT Trevor Goosby is questionable to play

Goosby opted to return to Austin for his redshirt junior season and is one of the nation's top left tackles. He suffered a knee injury two weeks ago, and while he's questionable for Saturday, Sarkisian said Goosby and left guard Laurence Seymore III practiced Monday.

"Both Trevor and Laurence practiced today, and I thought they both looked really good," Sarkisian said.

If the two are unable to play, Andre Cojoe will start at left tackle and Dylan Sikorski at left guard.

Sarkisian, Kinne have different philosophies

Kinne and Sarkisian are two of the best play-calling head coaches in the country. But though both coach in the Lone Star State, they run vastly different schemes.

Texas leans into a pro-style approach. Sarkisian has spent time in the NFL and uses a variation of the West Coast offense pioneered by Bill Walsh. Meanwhile, Kinne is from the Gus Malzahn coaching tree. Sarkisian compared Texas State's offense to Tennessee and LSU, mentioning the up-tempo approach and the wide receivers' big splits.

"It's tough to defend. It's unique in that way that you're not facing it every week, and so you've got to spend a little time to get ready for it," Sarkisian said.
